title: The Application of Latent Semantic Analysis to the Voynich Manuscript
authors: Colin Layfield and Lisa Fagin Davis
summary: The authors apply latent semantic analysis to short manuscript segments under three term-weighting schemes and compare adjacent with shuffled segment orders. A separate sliding-window analysis locates abrupt changes within the manuscript.
established: Adjacent segments showed greater cosine similarity than shuffled segment orders in the manuscript and the comparison texts. The artificial self-citation text also produced this basic pattern, with a different score distribution.

The lowest five percent of sliding-window scores included many Herbal page boundaries and disproportionate Currier A-to-B transitions. The Biological, Pharmaceutical, Zodiac and Stars sections had relatively few scores below this cutoff.

open.question: Can a self-citation or other nonlinguistic process with prespecified changes at page and section boundaries reproduce the distribution of the manuscript's local similarities and transition scores?
open.check: Compare the full score distribution and the fraction of low scores at section and Currier transitions under identical preprocessing and matched block layouts.
